title: Fix one-based pagination boundaries
prompt: The paginate API uses one-based page numbers. Fix the implementation so the first page, later pages, partial last pages and pages beyond the end work correctly. Preserve validation of positive page and page_size, return a new list, and do not mutate input. Change only pager.py.
grader:
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1])
from pager import paginate

items = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]
assert paginate(items, 1, 2) == [0, 1]
assert paginate(items, 2, 2) == [2, 3]
assert paginate(items, 3, 2) == [4]
assert paginate(items, 4, 2) == []
assert paginate([], 1, 2) == []
assert items == [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]
assert paginate(items, 1, 10) is not items
for page, size in ((0, 1), (-1, 1), (1, 0), (1, -1)):
    try:
        paginate(items, page, size)
    except ValueError:
        pass
    else:
        raise AssertionError("invalid pagination accepted")
print("NEIL_GRADER_COMPLETED")

title: Allocate the first available slug suffix
prompt: Fix unique_slug so an occupied base slug gets the lowest available numeric suffix starting at 2. Existing names may contain gaps, irrelevant names or high suffixes. Normalize titles with the current lowercase ASCII slug rules, use item for empty normalized titles, and leave the existing collection unchanged. Change only slugs.py.
grader:
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1])
from slugs import unique_slug

assert unique_slug("Hello World!", set()) == "hello-world"
assert unique_slug("Post", {"post", "post-2", "other"}) == "post-3"
assert unique_slug("Post", {"post", "post-3", "post-99"}) == "post-2"
assert unique_slug("...", {"item", "item-2"}) == "item-3"
existing = {"post", "post-2", "post-3"}
assert unique_slug("Post", existing) == "post-4"
assert existing == {"post", "post-2", "post-3"}
assert unique_slug("Fresh", {"fresh-2"}) == "fresh"
print("NEIL_GRADER_COMPLETED")
